notes: **Dehydration of alcohol:** $R-CH_2-CH_2-OH \xrightarrow{conc. H_2SO_4, 170Â°C} R-CH=CH_2 + H_2O$. Follows Saytzeff rule: more substituted alkene is major product.
**Dehydrohalogenation:** $R-CH_2-CH_2-X \xrightarrow{alc. KOH} R-CH=CH_2 + HX$. Removes HX from adjacent carbons.
**Catalytic hydrogenation of alkyne:** $R-C \equiv C-R' + 2H_2 \xrightarrow{Pd/BaSO_4, quinoline} R-CH=CH-R'$ (Lindlar catalyst gives cis-alkene).

**Addition of HX:** follows Markovnikov's rule: H adds to the carbon with more hydrogens. Example: $CH_3CH=CH_2 + HBr \rightarrow CH_3CHBrCH_3$ (major). Peroxide effect (anti-Markovnikov): $CH_3CH=CH_2 + HBr \xrightarrow{peroxide} CH_3CH_2CH_2Br$.
**Addition of $H_2O$:** acid-catalysed hydration: $CH_2=CH_2 + H_2O \xrightarrow{H^+} CH_3CH_2OH$. Follows Markovnikov rule.
**Ozonolysis:** $R-CH=CH-R' + O_3 \rightarrow R-CHO + R'-CHO$. Cleaves double bond to carbonyl compounds.
